$comment: The rules every SDK reads from registry.json, as cases each SDK runs. `cloneFormat`: the format a clone of a resource takes: its source's base media type when that is one a person can author, and text/plain otherwise, since a clone opens where a person writes. `storageFileName`: the name a resource's content is stored under: its title in lower case, every run of characters that are not a to z or 0 to 9 made one hyphen, none at either end, and then the format's extension. A `file://` storage URI is that name behind the scheme. `textSource`: where the text of a resource of a format comes from, and the two things that follow from it. A format's parameters and its letter case are not part of its type. A type the registry lists answers as its row says: `decode`, its bytes are its text; `pdf-text-layer`, its text is derived by reading its bytes; `none`, it has no text. A type the registry does not list is `decode` when it is a `text/` type, and `none` otherwise. `yieldsGeometry` is whether that text comes with where each run of it is on a page: a text derived from a PDF does, and a decoded one does not. `derivesText` is whether the text is derived from the bytes, and not decoded from them. Every case states all three: `textSourceOf`, `yieldsGeometryOf` and `derivesTextOf`, each spelled in its SDK's convention (`textSourceOf` is text_source_of).

cloneFormat.why: an authorable source keeps its type
parameters are not part of the type
case is not part of the type
a type nobody authors falls back to plain text
so does a stored type that is text but not authorable
so does a type the registry does not have
and a source that states none

storageFileName.why: lower case, spaces to hyphens, the format's extension
storageFileName.name: My Document

storageFileName.why: a run of anything else is one hyphen, and none is left at either end
storageFileName.name: Hello, World!

storageFileName.why: letters outside a to z are not kept
storageFileName.name: Café Über 2

storageFileName.why: a name with nothing to keep is the extension alone
a hyphen in the name is a character like any other that is not kept
storageFileName.name: -a--b-

storageFileName.why: lower case is Unicode's: the Kelvin sign is a k
storageFileName.name: K2

textSource.why: a text type the registry lists: its bytes are its text
a type the registry lists as decoded need not be a text/ type
a PDF's text is derived by reading its bytes, and comes with where each run of it is on a page
nor has an archive, which the registry lists too
parameters are not part of the type
case is not part of the type
a text/ type the registry does not list is decoded: the type says of itself that it is text
and so is one written in capitals and with parameters, which are not part of that type either
any other type the registry does not list has no text
an empty format is no type, and has no text
